text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on June 19 in history:

1566 - King James VI of Scotland born in Edinburgh. In 1567 at the age of one, he became James VI of Scotland. In 1603 he became James I of England and thus became the first King to rule both Scotland and England.
1623 - Blaise Pascal, French mathematician, born. He invented one of the first calculators and contributed greatly to the development of mathematical theories including calculus.
1669 - Michael Wisniowiecki who came from Lithuania, was elected King of Poland after successive struggles over the succession.
1829 - Sir Robert Peel introduced an act of parliament which established the London Metropolitan police.
1846 - The first baseball game with set rules was played at the Elysian fields in Hoboken New Jersey in the United States.
1867 - Maximilian, Emperor of Mexico, having been abandoned by Napoleon III of France, was captured and executed by supporters of Juarez.
1896 - Bessie Wallis Warfield was born in Blue Ridge Summit in Pennsylvania. Later the Duchess of Windsor, she married British King Edward VIII who renounced the throne for her in 1936.
1906 - Sir Ernest Boris Chain, chemist born in Berlin. Best known for his pioneering work with penicilin, he shared the Nobel prize for Physiology or Medicine with Alexander Fleming in 1945.
1921 - Louis Jourdan, French actor of stage and screen, born as Louis Gendre. He starred in "Gigi", "Three Coins in a Fountain" as well as "Dracula" on television.
1942 - Germany announced it had executed General Elias, former prime minister of the Czech puppet government.
1944 - The Battle of the Philippines Sea began when the Japanese fleet attacked U.S. ships protecting a landing at Saipan This resulted in considerable air and sea losses for Japan.
1947 - Salman Rushdie, Indian writer, born. Famed for his "Satanic Verses" which caused Iran to declare a Fatwa or decree calling for the author's death for blasphemy.
1953 - Julius and Ethel Rosenberg were executed by electric chair at Sing Sing prison for spying for the Soviet Union. They were the first married couple to be executed in the United States.
1961 - An 1899 agreement by which Britain was reponsible for overseeing Kuwaiti foreign policy was terminated thus making Kuwait a fully independent state.
1961 - Evidence was found for the first time proving the existence of Pontius Pilot when a slab with his name on it was found by an Italian dig at Caesarea in Israel.
1964 - U.S. Civil rights bill was passed by the House of Representatives. It was passed by the Senate on July 2.
1970 - The Soyuz-9 spacecraft landed safely back in the USSR after a record 17 days in space in Earth orbit.
1983 - Lixian-nian was chosen as China's first President since 1969.
1993 - Nobel prize winning author, Sir William Golding died in Truro in Cornwall. The British writer was famous for his novels "Lord of the Flies" and "Rites of Passage". He was 81.
1994 - Michel Rocard resigned as head of the French Socialist party after the movement's national council voted a no-confidence vote against him.
